title: Link a sliver to its parent slice with a parent field
lead: An item gains an optional `parent` field naming the slice it is a sliver of. A sliver is a small child item (size S, effort 1) that a relay orchestrator carves out of a larger slice so a cheaper implementer can take it. This slice adds the link and the views; s274 adds the readiness and finish rules, and s275 the relay guidance.
findings_note: owner request, session 2026-10-14: slivers (parent:child) for relays

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The owner asked on 2026-10-14 for slivers to be tracked items with a parent:child relationship, one level deep. Today the only item-to-item links are `depends_on` and `discovered_from`; neither says "this is part of that". s258's split parts are untracked, so a sliver's status, notes and attempts have nowhere to live.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/model.py`: `Item.parent` next to `discovered_from` (around line 237), in `to_dict`/`from_dict` in fixed key order, with a validator like `_discovered_from`. Bump `SCHEMA_VERSION` (line 15) from 8 to 9, as s210 bumped 4 to 5 for `discovered_from`.
- `src/slicer/ops.py`: `add` accepts and validates `parent` (as at line 301); `_blockers` refuses `remove`/`retire`/`purge` of an item that still has slivers unless `--force` (as at lines 2040-2056); `_reclaim_check` will not free an id that a `parent` field names (as at line 2090); `set`/`edit` can set and clear it.
- `src/slicer/cli.py`: `add --parent ID`, `list --parent ID` (filter as `list --discovered-from` at line 1701), and the field on `set`. `show ID` lists the item's slivers with id, status and title, in text and `--json`.
- `src/slicer/outline.py`: `parent` in `KEYS` (line 41) and the item spec, so `import` files several slivers in one batch.
- `src/slicer/verify.py` (line 162) and `src/slicer/mergeindex.py` (line 267): unknown parent, parent that has a parent, and self-parent are errors with stable codes.
- `src/slicer/render.py`: the slice header names its parent (as line 152 does for discovered from) and the table row carries it (line 245).
- `docs/agents.md` (JSON shapes), `docs/commands.md`, `docs/import.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` where s210 touched them, `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]`.
- `tests/test_parent.py` (new), modelled on `tests/test_provenance.py`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_Add_WithParent_StoresAndRoundTrips`: `add --parent s1` stores the field; to_dict/from_dict round-trips it byte for byte.
- `test_Add_UnknownParent_Refused`, `test_Add_ParentThatHasParent_Refused`, `test_Set_SelfParent_Refused`: each exits 2 with its stable code and writes nothing.
- `test_Check_UnknownParent_ReportsError` and the nested and self cases via `verify`.
- `test_MergeIndex_ParentDroppedOnOneSide_Reported`: a merge that leaves a dangling parent is reported.
- `test_Remove_ParentWithSlivers_RefusedWithoutForce`, `test_Purge_ParentNamedBySliver_KeepsId`.
- `test_Show_Parent_ListsSlivers` (text and JSON), `test_List_ParentFilter_ReturnsSlivers`.
- `test_Import_ParentKey_FilesSliversInOneBatch`, including a parent filed earlier in the same file.
- `test_Render_Sliver_NamesParent`.
- `test_Load_SchemaTooNew_Refused` still holds at version 9.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests above and watch them go red.
2. Add the model field, validator and schema bump.
3. Add `ops`, `cli`, `outline`, `verify`, `mergeindex` and `render` support, following each `discovered_from` site named in Files.
4. Update the docs and CHANGELOG.
5. Mutation-check each new test.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- The full suite passes on Python 3.11+.
- `slicer check` and `git diff --check` pass; this repo's state loads at schema 9 and re-renders without drift beyond the version.
- `docs/agents.md` shows `parent` in every JSON shape that shows `discovered_from`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Worktree `.worktrees/s273`, branch `feature/s273-parent-field`. Commit only on the branch. Merging and pushing wait for the owner.

sections.heading: Boundary
sections.body:
- One level only: an item with a parent cannot itself be a parent, and an item cannot be its own parent.
- `parent` is a reference, not a dependency. Readiness and finish rules belong to s274; this slice does not change `next`, `handoff` or `done`.
- Follow the `discovered_from` pattern from s210 (commit 07c37ef) everywhere it applies. No new mechanism where that one fits.
